faq.a: Mesut is associated with the Arabic form مَسْعُود, whose core sense is mesut; fortunate, happy (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Mesut?
faq.a: Mesut is associated with Arabic. Mesut is the Turkish form of Arabic مَسْعُود (Masʿūd), meaning 'fortunate, happy'.
Yes — the underlying form مَسْعُود is Arabic.
Mesut can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Mesut should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Masʿūd is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Mesut mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Mesut is rendered مسعود and carries the sense مسعود، خوشبخت.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Mesut, mesut. Script forms are مسعود, مَسْعُود, मसूद.

faq.q: Is Mesut a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
